_instructions: Copy this file to output/products/<source-slug>--<product-slug>.json and fill it in.
Use this template when a source can't run through the automated pipeline (node run.js) —
a PDF, a paywalled article, a screenshot, or your own notes from a site. If the source is
an ordinary webpage or YouTube video the pipeline can fetch itself, add it to data/sources.json
and run `node run.js <slug>` instead — that path needs no manual entry at all.
Once this file is saved into output/products/, it is indistinguishable from an automated
record: `npm run preview` will render it, and `node src/buildReports.js` will pull it into
the scored report and the coverage leaderboard, same as any other source.
status must be exactly one of: evidenced | brand_claim_only | gap
evidenced         at least one claim backed by something other than the seller itself
brand_claim_only  every claim on this dimension traces back to the product's own seller
gap               nothing found for this dimension — leave claims empty and fill gap_note
evidence_kind must be exactly one of: tested | cited_third_party | brand_claim_repeated | anecdotal
tested                 the reviewer personally measured or instrumented this
cited_third_party      the reviewer cites a study, filing, or independent source
brand_claim_repeated   the reviewer is repeating what the seller itself says
anecdotal              a forum post, owner report, or similar uncorroborated account
Do not fill in a numeric score anywhere in this file. Scores are computed later by
extension/scoring/pillars.js from evidence_kind and status — that's what keeps every
product on the same rules. If you're tempted to write a number here, that's a sign the
claim belongs in reviewer_verdict as context, not as a claim.
Delete this _instructions block before committing the finished file.
